name: Glycogen Storage Disease Due to Glycogen Branching Enzyme Deficiency, Adult Neuromuscular Form

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Adult Polyglucosan Body Disease

criteria.description: Progressive adult-onset neuromuscular symptoms including muscle weakness and atrophy
Presence of polyglucosan bodies in muscle biopsy or nerve tissue
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GBE1 gene encoding glycogen branching enzyme
Electromyography showing myopathic and/or neurogenic changes
Reduced glycogen branching enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive adult-onset neuromuscular symptoms plus either histopathological confirmation of polyglucosan bodies or pathogenic GBE1 gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and muscle biopsy; enzyme assay may support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Polyglucosan body accumulation in muscle and nerve tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Detected via biopsy, hallmark of disease
searchTerms: build-up of abnormal sugar bodies in muscle and nerve
accumulation of abnormal glycogen in muscle and nerve

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy
searchTerms: gradual weakness and wasting of distal muscles
progressive muscle loss in hands and feet

pathognomonic.notes: Urinary symptoms due to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: adult onset bladder control problems from nerve damage
loss of bladder control due to nerve issues

common.notes: Upper motor neuron signs may be present

occasional.notes: Due to autonomic nervous system involvement
May contribute to dyspnea on exertion

laboratory: Reduced glycogen branching enzyme activity in leukocytes or fibroblasts
Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration and atrophy
Brain MRI may show mild white matter changes
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating polyglucosan bodies with PAS-positive staining
Electromyography showing mixed myopathic and neurogenic features

distinguishingFeatures: Similar polyglucosan body accumulation but often with more prominent central nervous system involvement
Rapidly progressive motor neuron disease without polyglucosan bodies
Absence of glycogen branching enzyme deficiency
Different enzyme deficiencies (e.g., acid maltase deficiency in Pompe disease)

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Early autonomic dysfunction including urinary retention
Presence of polyglucosan bodies on muscle biopsy
references: DiMauro S, et al. Glycogen storage diseases: clinical and molecular aspects. Neurol Clin. 2019.
Orphanet: Adult polyglucosan body disease. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2021.
